cards.explanation: The answer is True. Ezekiel, a priest (Ezekiel 1:3), says, "…the Spirit entered me and set me on my feet…" He had just fallen facedown before the glory of the LORD (Ezekiel 1:28). I think a boost like that was welcome, friends.

The answer is them and their fathers, to this day. The LORD says it plainly: "To this very day they and their fathers have rebelled against Me." The fathers are in it too, not just the people standing in front of Ezekiel. He's walking into a long story, friends.

The answer is prophet. The LORD says, "…they will know that a prophet has been among them." He says it whether they listen or refuse to listen. So Ezekiel's job doesn't hang on how the crowd reacts, bakers. His job is to show up and speak.

The answer is False. The LORD never promises easy. He says, "Do not be afraid of their words or dismayed by their presence, though they are a rebellious house." The word is "though," so the rough crowd stays in the picture. Ezekiel is told not to fear them, friends.

The answer is speak. The LORD says, "But speak My words to them, whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are rebellious." Ezekiel's part is to say the words, friends. How people take them isn't his to control.

The answer is to open his mouth and eat what he's given. The LORD says, "Open your mouth and eat what I give you." It comes right after "Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house." So the answer to rebelling is opening up and taking what the LORD hands over, friends.

The answer is lamentation, mourning and woe. The words on the front and back of the scroll are "…lamentation, mourning, and woe." That's a lot of ink on both sides, bakers, and none of it light reading.

The answer is True. Ezekiel says, "So I opened my mouth, and He fed me the scroll." (Ezekiel 3:2) He opens his mouth, just as the LORD told him to. Earlier the LORD says, "Open your mouth and eat what I give you." (Ezekiel 2:8)

The answer is as sweet as honey! Ezekiel says, "…it was as sweet as honey in my mouth." The words on the scroll were lamentation, mourning and woe, and still it tasted sweet. I can't explain that one, friends, and I'm not going to pretend I can. I'll just say the text says it.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Surely if I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you." Peoples Ezekiel couldn't even understand would have listened, friends. Meanwhile his own people, who share his language, won't.

The answer is because they won't listen to the LORD. He says, "…the house of Israel will be unwilling to listen to you, since they are unwilling to listen to Me." The reason He gives is their unwillingness to listen to Him. They're turning away from the One who sent Ezekiel, friends.

The answer is Ezekiel's face and forehead. The LORD says, "…I will make your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads." Ezekiel gets a match for what he's facing, bakers. And since the LORD is the one doing the hardening, Ezekiel isn't going in with only his own strength.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I will make your forehead like a diamond, harder than flint." Then He adds, "Do not be afraid of them or dismayed at their presence…" That's a forehead you could stamp a thousand cookies with, friends.

The answer is exiles. The LORD says, "Go to your people, the exiles; speak to them and tell them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'" He's still told to speak, friends, whether they listen or refuse to listen.

The answer is the wings and wheels of the living creatures. Ezekiel says it was "…the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another and the sound of the wheels beside them, a great rumbling sound." Those living creatures were part of the vision that dropped him facedown (Ezekiel 1:28). I think that's a rumble he won't forget, bakers.

The answer is in bitterness and anger of spirit. Ezekiel says, "…I went in bitterness and in the anger of my spirit, with the strong hand of the LORD upon me." The text doesn't say why he felt that way, friends. It does say the strong hand of the LORD was upon him.

The answer is overwhelmed. Ezekiel says that for seven days he "…sat where they sat and remained there among them, overwhelmed." The text doesn't say why he was overwhelmed, friends. I think after the scroll and that rumble, it was a lot to take in.
